challenges.headline: Editing the total directly
challenges.premise: Users should be able to edit the reported total itself.
challenges.alternative: A total is the sum of underlying entries, so letting users overwrite it breaks that link. Recording each change as a separate adjustment line with an amount, account, period, author and reason keeps the total adding up, keeps the original figure visible, and lets a change be reversed.
challenges.consequence: A plain overwrite makes the report silently disagree with its own source data, weakens the audit trail, and leaves no way to reconcile later. Retrofitting traceability after launch is expensive.
challenges.recommendation: Settle with the client that an 'edit' means an adjustment entry, and allow an override only if they can name a case that an adjustment cannot cover. Even then, mark the figure visibly as overridden, with who and why.

challenges.headline: Editing after period close
challenges.premise: Users can change figures whenever they need to, with no mention of the period lifecycle.
challenges.alternative: Once a period is closed, route corrections to an adjustment in the next open period. Re-opening a closed period would be a separate, logged, restricted action, if allowed at all.
challenges.consequence: Changing a closed period invalidates exports and filings already produced from it. Each change then needs tracking down and re-communicating, and the finance team may be holding numbers that no longer match the system.
challenges.recommendation: Ask Finance which correction path they use today and decide whether re-opening is permitted before designing the workflow.

challenges.headline: Building a new export
challenges.premise: The finance team needs a new export of the edited figures.
challenges.alternative: The platform already exports to the accounting system. Extending that export to carry adjusted figures, with a clear flag separating raw from adjusted amounts, may meet the need without a second file format.
challenges.consequence: A second export doubles the formats to maintain and rounding conventions to reconcile. It also creates a risk that the two files disagree about the same period.
challenges.recommendation: Get a sample of what the finance team actually uses today and compare it with the existing export before scoping a new one.

If edits turn out to be overrides, reports stop tying back to source data and the audit trail has gaps that are costly to fix later.

Changes after close or after an export leave sent reports stale, and without a restatement mechanism the finance team may act on old numbers.

Make exports versioned, retained snapshots, so any file sent can be retrieved exactly as it was rather than regenerated.
Make adjustment approval circuits configurable per client, since these differ between clients.

Decide the closed-period path (next-period adjustment, or controlled re-open) and who may adjust, approve and close.

challenges.headline: Editing a derived total
challenges.premise: A reported total is a number users can simply edit.
challenges.alternative: Treat each correction as a new, attributed adjustment entry on the underlying data so the total still adds up and the original stays visible. An override that replaces the value is a different, riskier build and should be a deliberate choice, not the default.
challenges.consequence: An override makes the report silently disagree with its source entries, breaks reconciliation, and leaves a gap in the audit trail finance relies on at audit time.
challenges.recommendation: Get an explicit answer from finance on adjustment versus override before estimating; if override is truly wanted, require a visible marker, reason and approver.

challenges.headline: Building another export
challenges.premise: A new export for the finance team needs to be built.
challenges.alternative: The platform already has an export to the accounting system and a period review and close. The gap may be a field set, a format variant or an unused option rather than a new export. Reusing that export and adding versioning and adjustment visibility could be much smaller.
challenges.consequence: A parallel export duplicates the format contract, creates two sources for the same numbers, and doubles the maintenance on rounding and field mapping.
challenges.recommendation: Compare the current export to what finance actually receives and needs, and list the concrete gaps before committing to a new one.

challenges.headline: Unspecified 'users' editing
challenges.premise: Generic users may edit totals, with no distinction between viewing, adjusting and closing.
challenges.alternative: Define adjust and approve (and close) as separate rights, scoped by entity or cost center. The person who adjusts a figure should not be the one who approves it. This is a proposal to confirm, not something the client has said.
challenges.consequence: Open edit rights on financial figures create segregation-of-duties exposure and are typically found only at acceptance testing, when rework is costly.
challenges.recommendation: Name the roles that adjust and the roles that approve with finance management before design starts.

briefs.problem: Reported financial totals sometimes need correcting, and the finance team needs the resulting figures in a usable form, but the reason for the edits and today's workaround are unknown.
briefs.solution: A controlled way to correct reported figures, most likely as attributed adjustment entries on top of the derived totals, with an audit trail, and a versioned export for finance built on the existing accounting export.
introduces: an adjustment-entry capability (amount, account, period, author, reason) layered over derived totals
an approval and segregation-of-duties circuit for adjustments and period close
a field-level audit trail with previous and new values
versioned, retained export snapshots that can be reproduced later
restatement handling that flags exports and reports made stale by a later change
view/adjust/close rights scoped by entity or cost center

challenges.headline: Editing the total itself
challenges.premise: Users should be able to edit a reported total directly, as if it were a stored field.
challenges.alternative: Treat every change as an adjustment entry that sits beside the operational entries, so the total is always the sum of its lines and the edit stays attributed and reversible. Reports can then show both actuals and actuals including adjustments.
challenges.consequence: A direct override replaces the derived value, so the report silently stops tying back to its own source data. This is hard to detect and expensive to unpick at audit time.
challenges.recommendation: Get the requester to confirm adjustment versus override before any estimate. Default to adjustment, and treat override as an exception that needs an explicit decision and a visible marker.

challenges.headline: Is editing the right fix?
challenges.premise: Wrong or incomplete totals should be corrected at the report level.
challenges.alternative: If the cause is bad source data, correcting it at source and letting the aggregation recompute keeps every report and export consistent. Report-level adjustments are for genuine finance judgement, such as accruals and reclassifications.
challenges.consequence: Building report-level editing for what are really source-data problems adds a second place where numbers can be wrong, and the two will drift apart.
challenges.recommendation: Ask the requester for the last few real cases where a total was wrong and how each was fixed. Use them to split source fixes from finance adjustments before scoping.

challenges.headline: A new export versus the existing one
challenges.premise: The finance team needs an export of the figures, as if none existed.
challenges.alternative: The platform already exports to the accounting system. Extending that export to include adjustments, with versioning and retention, may cover the need at a fraction of the cost of a new one.
challenges.consequence: A parallel export creates two sources of truth for finance and doubles the field-mapping and format maintenance per client.
challenges.recommendation: Establish what the current export lacks, and whether the finance team's consumer is the accounting system or a human reading a file, before designing anything new.

complexity_reasons: adjustment model on top of derived totals, with separate views of raw and adjusted figures
export as a versioned contract with a downstream consumer
briefs.cost_driver: the adjustment, approval and restatement model around period close
risks: Aggregation is shared by every report, export and dashboard, so adding adjustments to it can shift numbers elsewhere.
A silent override would leave the report disagreeing with its source data and fail at audit.
An export may be rejected downstream if format, rounding or encoding differ from what the consumer expects.
Exports and published reports go stale when a figure changes after they were sent, and nobody is told.
Segregation of duties and entity-scoped rights are likely to be missed until acceptance testing.
Cut-off, FX and rounding conventions vary by client and are unstated, so totals may not tie out.

opportunities.text: Build adjustments as a general mechanism feeding the existing aggregation layer, so any report or dashboard can show actuals with or without adjustments.
Extend the existing accounting export with versioning and retention rather than adding a second export path.
Reuse the platform's approval-circuit pattern for adjustment approval and period re-open, configurable per client.
Turn the audit trail into a reconciliation view showing whether a report still ties back to its source.

next_steps: Hold a short session with finance to settle adjustment versus override, and review recent real corrections to see whether source fixes would remove most of the need.
Establish what the current accounting export lacks, who consumes it and in what format, and whether sent exports must be retrievable exactly.
Settle the rules for closed periods (next-period adjustment versus controlled re-open), approval, and who may view, adjust and close, including segregation of duties.
Only then estimate and slice the build: adjustments with audit trail first, export versioning and restatement flags second.

decisions.decision: Treat reported totals as derived values; any change is recorded as an attributed adjustment unless an override is explicitly approved
decisions.why: Keeps the report tied to its source data and auditable.
decisions.alternative: Direct override of the displayed total.
decisions.tradeoff: More build effort than a simple edit field, in exchange for a report that still ties out at audit.

decisions.decision: Closed periods stay frozen; corrections go to the next open period unless a controlled, logged re-open is approved
decisions.why: Re-opening invalidates everything already exported or filed.
decisions.tradeoff: Corrections show up in a later period, in exchange for stable filed figures.

decisions.decision: Exports are versioned and retained snapshots, not regenerated on demand
decisions.why: Finance must be able to show exactly what was sent.
decisions.alternative: Regenerate the file whenever it is requested.
decisions.tradeoff: Storage and a retention policy to manage, in exchange for reproducibility.

decisions.decision: The feature extends the existing aggregation, period close and accounting export rather than creating a new product
